status: Scoped serialized recovery and acknowledged retry qualified locally; broader production readiness remains active.
behavior: Deleted-wallet restoration shares the vault queue with local import, wallet removal, password change and TON recovery. Duplicate restores serialize; a preceding explicit import retains its newer record and restoration reports already_in_wallet.

Detached key records and primary storage/public identities are checked before writing. Every account entry, including ECDSA legacy account-id keys, must have a valid shape and match its storage identity. Legacy ECDSA copies remain stored but are not loaded; inert archivedAccount entries remain exact. TON public key must derive the archived address. These are encrypted-record/identity checks, not proof that every old record decrypts under the current password.

A single queued grouped mutation rereads the archive and every target record. Any occupied differing record or live primary/linked pair rejects the entire restoration without partial writes. Existing exact durable copies from a failed archive-removal attempt may be reused; only absent records are written.

The recovery archive is removed only after account/TON writes are acknowledged. Live pairs and TON subjects publish inside the acknowledged commit callback, including retry of identical already-written records. Publication uses the installed keyring addPair/accounts.add with an already-persisted store, avoiding ui-keyring loadAccount additional unacknowledged writes. Account access rescans older-password records.

Chrome still uses two acknowledged operations for record write and archive deletion. A failed deletion retains the archive and durable copies without live publication; explicit retry completes publication. Existing restart behavior loads the durable copies normally. The unchanged IndexedDB grouped adapter provides one transaction but was not exercised in a real browser for this slice.

newTests.scope: Actual installed keyring, KeyringService, TON seed encryption and controlled Chrome callbacks: import/duplicate concurrency, acknowledged failure/retry, linked collision, malformed current records, storage/public-key mismatches, nonredundant publication and real signing/phrase proof.

historicalTests.scope: Real2.6.3/3.0.x storage fixtures across fresh module graphs with inherited keyring stand-in; ECDSA stand-in adds installed addPair API. Included in final full suite. Intermediate focused-v1 passed15 tests before six additional validation regressions were added.

chrome.scope: Existing removal/recovery harness rebuilt on final source: trusted create/select/remove/list/restore/export handlers, actual Chrome storage and two observed worker replacements across four native curves, TON, linked EVM and public mobile addresses. No browser failure injection or relay negotiation.

independentReview.method: Read-only production, tests, exact adapter and installed-keyring publication review. Reviewer did not modify web code or run tests. Source files matched exact Git objects; final test/build/browser qualification remains root responsibility.

findings.description: The initial candidate used loadableAccountRecords before validation. An empty/missing encoded field or scalar linked record was silently skipped while all records were restored and the recovery archive consumed, reporting success without the linked pair.
findings.reproduced: Root preserved three failures against ad077c5b (empty, missing, scalar linked records).
findings.disposition: Final36c5aa00 validates every account entry before any write. Unknown keys, malformed record/meta, empty encoding and storage-key/public-identity mismatches reject. Legacy ECDSA account-id keys are explicitly recognized and validated; archivedAccount copies stay inert. Three new negative cases require unchanged durable recovery and no pair publication.

reviewConclusions: Restore holds the same vault queue as import, password rotation and native removal, preventing the earlier read/replace overwrite race inside this service.

One grouped store transformation re-reads the recovery copy and all destination keys. Conflicting live pairs or different durable bytes refuse restoration; identical bytes left by an acknowledged-write/failed-archive-removal attempt are safely reused on retry.

Detached pairs and TON public identity are prepared before consuming the recovery copy. In-memory publication occurs only after the grouped operation acknowledges; alreadyPersistedAccountStore prevents a second unacknowledged ui-keyring write.

Actual installed-keyring tests cover import ordering, failed write and archive deletion retry, linked-key collision, duplicate restore, malformed account and TON identity; historical ECDSA fixture adds the real backend addPair path.
limits: This restores exact encrypted records; older-password keys remain locked/recoverable through existing account-access scans. It does not prove decrypted private material against every archived header or recover lost passwords.
Chrome set/remove remains two durable calls, not a crash-atomic transaction. An interrupted attempt can leave exact destination records and archive together; explicit retry handles that state.
Cross-worker/cross-tab concurrency, whole reset, broader password/storage lifecycle and final selection/navigation durability beyond the existing awaited caller are separate gates.
No real relay, hardware/device recovery or physical accessibility claim.
Final frozen36c5aa00 full suite, build, type/lint and real Chrome rerun must be pinned by root; historical ad077 qualification is not substituted.

preservedDiagnostics.note: Preceding import disrupted; native/TON retry reports success without live wallet; extra unacknowledged write; linked-key partial recovery; concurrent duplicate success. Failed account write already retained archive. TON proof call initially omitted its required public-key argument; baseline TON failure is earlier at absent live wallet, and final proof uses the actual restored public key.

Independent review reproduced silently filtered linked account with empty/missing encoded field or scalar record, consuming archive and reporting success. Final validates every loadable account entry before storage.
Intermediate full2890pass18skip and build successful, before malformed-record review fix. Final source is requalified separately.
Test decryptTonSeed omitted required public-key argument; obsolete tonStore import became unused. Both corrected before final qualification.

limits: Restore retains exact archived encryption, even if an earlier password is required. It does not reencrypt or silently claim current-password access; existing Account access recovery remains necessary. Only public unfunded fixtures were used.

Chrome write/archive removal is not crash atomic. A terminated or failed operation can leave both active storage and an archive; a restart may load active records while hiding the redundant archive. No physical disk/power-failure durability claim.
Same-context vault/store serialization is qualified. Whole-wallet reset, password partial-failure recovery, cross-worker/tab/external storage mutations and actual browser IndexedDB remain open gates.

Record equality uses serialized JSON. Property-order changes in externally modified records can conservatively reject restoration; no differing record is overwritten. Inert archivedAccount contents are preserved without decryption/validation.

This checkpoint adds no UI, real relay/phone, physical accessibility, final historical-artifact upgrade, private-chain send or production publication acceptance. Broader protocol and native work remain active.
